af og til.explanation: "Af og til" means "now and then". Compare "Jeg drikker kaffe hver dag" (I drink coffee every day) with "Jeg drikker kaffe af og til" (I drink coffee now and then).

forms.da: jeg går i biografen af og til
forms.en: I go to the cinema now and then

sentence.da: Jeg spiser ikke kage hver dag, kun **af og til**.
sentence.en: I do not eat cake every day, only now and then.

aflyst.explanation: "Aflyst" means "cancelled", for example a train, a flight or an event that will not take place. It is different from "forsinket" (delayed): a delayed train still comes, a cancelled one does not.

sentence.da: Toget er **aflyst**, så vi tager bussen.
sentence.en: The train is cancelled, so we take the bus.

sentence.da: Løver og elefanter lever i **Afrika**.
sentence.en: Lions and elephants live in Africa.

afsted.explanation: "Afsted" means "off" or "away", for leaving a place. Compare "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home) with "Jeg skal afsted" (I have to go / I am heading off).

sentence.da: Bussen kører om fem minutter, så vi skal **afsted** nu.
sentence.en: The bus leaves in five minutes, so we have to go now.

aftensmad.explanation: "Aftensmad" means "dinner". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "mad" (food).

sentence.da: Om aftenen spiser vi **aftensmad** sammen.
sentence.en: In the evening we eat dinner together.

aldrig.explanation: "Aldrig" means "never". Compare "Jeg drikker altid kaffe" (I always drink coffee) with "Jeg drikker aldrig kaffe" (I never drink coffee). Do not add "ikke" (not) next to it.

sentence.da: Hun spiser **aldrig** kød, kun grøntsager.
sentence.en: She never eats meat, only vegetables.

alene.explanation: "Alene" means "alone" or "on your own". Compare "Jeg bor alene" (I live alone, nobody else is in my home) with "Jeg er ensom" (I feel lonely, which is a sad feeling).

sentence.da: Jeg bor **alene**, der er ingen andre i huset.
sentence.en: I live alone, there is nobody else in the house.

alkohol.explanation: "Alkohol" means "alcohol". Danish does not put "en" (a) in front of it: "Jeg drikker ikke alkohol" (I do not drink alcohol).

sentence.da: Der er **alkohol** i øl og vin, men ikke i juice.
sentence.en: There is alcohol in beer and wine, but not in juice.

alle.explanation: "Alle" means "everyone" or "all". Compare "Alle er her" (Everyone is here) with "Alt er her" (Everything is here).

sentence.da: **Alle** er her: mor, far og børnene.
sentence.en: Everyone is here: mum, dad and the children.

allerede.explanation: "Allerede" means "already". Compare "Han er her ikke endnu" (He is not here yet) with "Han er allerede her" (He is already here, earlier than expected). Also "Jeg har allerede spist" (I have already eaten).

sentence.da: Klokken er kun otte, men han er **allerede** på arbejde.
sentence.en: It is only eight o'clock, but he is already at work.

allergisk.explanation: "Allergisk" means "allergic". To say what you are allergic to, add "over for" (to / towards): "Jeg er allergisk over for nødder" (I am allergic to nuts).

sentence.da: Nødder gør mig syg, for jeg er **allergisk**.
sentence.en: Nuts make me sick, because I am allergic.

alt.explanation: "Alt" means "everything" or "all". Compare "Alle er her" (Everyone is here) with "Alt er her" (Everything is here). "Alt for" means "far too": "alt for dyrt" (far too expensive).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke huske noget. Jeg har glemt **alt**.
sentence.en: I can't remember anything. I have forgotten everything.

altid.explanation: "Altid" means "always". Compare "Jeg er aldrig træt" (I am never tired) with "Jeg er altid træt" (I am always tired).

sentence.da: Jeg står **altid** op klokken seks, hver eneste dag.
sentence.en: I always get up at six o'clock, every single day.

altså.explanation: "Altså" means "so" or "then", when you sum up what was just said: "Han er syg, så han kommer altså ikke" (He is sick, so he is not coming then). It also adds emphasis, like "really": compare "Det er dyrt" (It is expensive) with "Det er altså dyrt!" (It really is expensive!).

sentence.da: Hvad? Det koster tusind kroner? Det er **altså** for dyrt!
sentence.en: What? It costs a thousand kroner? That is really too expensive!

amerikansk.explanation: "Amerikansk" means "American", used for things from the USA. It is written with a small letter, where English "American" has a capital.

sentence.da: Filmen kommer fra USA, så den er **amerikansk**.
sentence.en: The film comes from the USA, so it is American.

anden.explanation: "Anden" means "second" and also "other". Compare "min første dag" (my first day) with "min anden dag" (my second day). "Den anden bil" can mean "the second car" or "the other car", and the situation tells you which. In dates: "den anden juni" (the second of June).

sentence.da: Det er min **anden** dag i Danmark; i går var den første.
sentence.en: It is my second day in Denmark; yesterday was the first.

appelsinjuice.explanation: "En appelsinjuice" means "an orange juice". It is built from "appelsin" (orange) and "juice" (juice).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **appelsinjuice**. Den smager af appelsin.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of orange juice. It tastes of orange.

april.explanation: "April" means "April". Danish writes month names with a small letter, where English has a capital: "i april" (in April). "Aprilsnar" means "April fool", built from "april" and "nar" (fool).

sentence.da: Efter marts kommer **april**, og så kommer maj.
sentence.en: After March comes April, and then comes May.

arabisk.explanation: "Arabisk" means "Arabic", and it is used for the language and for things from the Arab world. It is written with a small letter, where English "Arabic" has a capital: "Hun taler arabisk" (She speaks Arabic).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Egypten og taler **arabisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Egypt and speaks Arabic.

asien.explanation: "Asien" means "Asia": "Hun har rejst meget i Asien" (She has travelled a lot in Asia).

sentence.da: Kina og Japan ligger i **Asien**.
sentence.en: China and Japan are in Asia.

at arbejde.explanation: "At arbejde" means "to work": "Jeg arbejder på et hospital" (I work at a hospital). "Et arbejde" also means "a job" or "work" itself: "Jeg har meget arbejde" (I have a lot of work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **arbejde** på kontoret fra ni til fem.
sentence.en: I have to work at the office from nine to five.

atten.explanation: "Atten" means "eighteen". For age: "Jeg er atten år" (I am eighteen years old).

sentence.da: Sytten, **atten**, nitten – nu kan jeg tælle!
sentence.en: Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen – now I can count!

august.explanation: "August" means "August". Danish writes month names with a small letter, so you write "i august" (in August), not "i August".

sentence.da: Efter juli kommer **august**, og så starter skolen igen.
sentence.en: After July comes August, and then school starts again.

australien.explanation: "Australien" means "Australia". Use "i" (in) for being there and "til" (to) for going there: "Jeg bor i Australien" (I live in Australia), "Jeg rejser til Australien" (I am travelling to Australia).

sentence.da: Kænguruer lever i **Australien**, langt fra Danmark.
sentence.en: Kangaroos live in Australia, far from Denmark.

en adresse.explanation: "En adresse" means "an address", the street and number where someone lives. You ask "Hvad er din adresse?" (What is your address?).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver min **adresse** på brevet: Vestergade 12.
sentence.en: I write my address on the letter: Vestergade 12.

en afgang.explanation: "En afgang" means "a departure", the time a train, bus or plane leaves. You can ask "Hvornår er næste afgang?" (When is the next departure?).

sentence.da: Næste **afgang** er klokken ni, og toget kører til Aarhus.
sentence.en: The next departure is at nine, and the train goes to Aarhus.

en aftale.explanation: "En aftale" means "an appointment" or "an agreement". An appointment: "en aftale med tandlægen" (an appointment with the dentist). A deal: "Det er en aftale!" (It's a deal!).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **aftale** med lægen.
sentence.en: I have an appointment with the doctor.

en aften.explanation: "En aften" means "an evening". Useful phrases are "i aften" (tonight), "om aftenen" (in the evening, as a habit) and "god aften" (good evening).

sentence.da: Solen går ned, og så er det **aften**.
sentence.en: The sun goes down, and then it is evening.

en agurk.explanation: "En agurk" means "a cucumber". Pickled ones are "syltede agurker" (pickled cucumbers).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **agurk** til salaten.
sentence.en: I am cutting a cucumber for the salad.

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish often says "the elbow" where English says "my elbow": "Jeg har slået albuen" is literally "I have hit the elbow", meaning "I have hit my elbow". "Min albue" is also fine.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i min **albue**, så jeg kan ikke bøje armen.
sentence.en: My elbow hurts, so I can't bend my arm.

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age", how old someone is. To ask, Danes say "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?), because "alder" sounds formal, like on a form.

sentence.da: På blanketten skal du skrive din **alder**.
sentence.en: On the form you have to write your age.

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy". In a restaurant you can say "Jeg har en allergi" (I have an allergy) or be specific, as in "Jeg har en nøddeallergi" (I have a nut allergy).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **allergi**, så jeg må ikke spise nødder.
sentence.en: I have an allergy, so I must not eat nuts.

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance". In an emergency you can say "Jeg har brug for en ambulance" (I need an ambulance).

sentence.da: Han er meget syg. Ring efter en **ambulance**!
sentence.en: He is very sick. Call for an ambulance!

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American", a person from the USA.

sentence.da: Hun er **amerikaner**, men bor i Danmark.
sentence.en: She is American but lives in Denmark.

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple". Pineapple juice is "ananasjuice" (pineapple juice).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en sød, gul **ananas** i stykker.
sentence.en: I cut a sweet, yellow pineapple into pieces.

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". Watch out: "anden" also means "the other" or "second", as in "den anden" (the other one), so the rest of the sentence shows which is meant.

sentence.da: Der svømmer en **and** på søen, og den siger kvak.
sentence.en: A duck is swimming on the lake, and it says quack.

en ankomst.explanation: "En ankomst" means "an arrival", the time a train, plane or person gets somewhere: "Hvornår er ankomsten?" (When is the arrival?)

sentence.da: Vores **ankomst** er klokken tolv, så kom og hent os.
sentence.en: Our arrival is at twelve, so come and pick us up.

en app.explanation: "En app" means "an app", a small program on your phone or tablet. To download one Danes say "at hente en app" (literally "to fetch an app"), and to open it "at åbne appen" (to open the app).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **app** til min telefon.
sentence.en: I am downloading an app for my phone.

en appelsin.explanation: "En appelsin" means "an orange", the fruit. The colour orange is "orange": "en orange bold" (an orange ball).

sentence.da: Jeg skrællede en **appelsin** til børnene.
sentence.en: I peeled an orange for the children.

en arm.explanation: "En arm" means "an arm". Danish often says "the arm" where English says "her arm": "Hun har brækket armen" is literally "She has broken the arm", meaning "She has broken her arm".

sentence.da: Hånden sidder for enden af din **arm**.
sentence.en: Your hand is at the end of your arm.

en avis.explanation: "En avis" means "a newspaper", printed pages with the day's news. "At læse avisen" means "to read the paper". Do not mix it up with "et blad" (a magazine).

sentence.da: Min far læser en **avis** og drikker kaffe hver morgen.
sentence.en: My dad reads a newspaper and drinks coffee every morning.

et ansigt.explanation: "Et ansigt" means "a face". "Vask dit ansigt" means "Wash your face" and "et glad ansigt" means "a happy face".

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mit **ansigt** med vand og sæbe.
sentence.en: I wash my face with water and soap.

et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy", the shop where you buy medicine. The person working there is "en farmaceut" (a pharmacist). Say "på apoteket" for "at the pharmacy".

sentence.da: Jeg køber medicin på et **apotek**.
sentence.en: I buy medicine at a pharmacy.

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job" or "work". Danes say "på arbejde" (at work): "Jeg er på arbejde" means "I am at work", and "at gå på arbejde" means "to go to work".

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **arbejde** nu.
sentence.en: I have to go to work now.
